title: Linking through unique identifier
description: Parent user shares email address during registration, which serves as a unique identifier allowing data linkage to the individual.

title: Processing of identified data
description: Authentication service processes email as part of parent registration, which constitutes identified information.

title: Sensitive data type collection
description: Registration collects password and profileImage, which are highly sensitive data types beyond basic authentication needs.

title: Unawareness as user sharing personal data
description: Parent user shares email, password, profileImage and userType without explicit indications of awareness about subsequent processing.

title: Violation of data minimization
description: ProfileImage and userType may exceed the minimum data necessary for authentication service registration.

title: Processing of identified data by source
description: Authentication Service (P1) shares email which constitutes identified information when writing the new parent user record.

title: Storage of identified data at destination
description: User Database (DS1) receives and stores email which is identified information for the parent user.

title: Identifier in data flow
description: The data flow DF2 carries email as a unique reference to the identity of the data subject.

title: Sensitive data type stored
description: Hashed password is a sensitive data type being written and stored beyond basic identification needs, even if required for authentication.

title: Unique identifier linking
description: Email acts as a unique identifier in the flow enabling potential linking of the parent user data.

title: Processing of identified data for login
description: The Authentication Service (P1) requests user email as part of reading credentials to perform parent login check, which is identified information.

title: Sensitive password data type in flow
description: The data flow involves password (highly sensitive data type) for the credential check, which may be disclosed or transmitted beyond strict necessity if not properly protected.

title: Propagation of credentials to datastore
description: User credentials are made accessible to the User Database as part of the read operation for authentication.

title: Processing of identified login credentials
description: Authentication Service receives email address as part of login credentials, which constitutes identified information being processed for authentication.

title: Transmission of sensitive password data
description: The data flow transmits a password, which is a highly sensitive data type that could lead to disclosure if the channel is not adequately protected.

title: Processing of identified parent email data
description: The Authentication Service processes the parent's email address, which is identified information, during child login.

title: Sensitive child profile data disclosure
description: Child profile selection involves processing potentially sensitive personal data of a minor beyond minimal authentication needs.

title: Child unawareness of data processing
description: The child user may be unaware of the collection and processing of parent email and profile data during login.

title: Invalid consent for child data
description: Login involving child profile and parent email may not ensure valid parental consent as required for processing children's personal data.
uncertainty_note: Child-specific consent rules assumed based on context of child login.

title: Linking via parent email identifier
description: The data flow transmits parent email which serves as a unique identifier linking the child profile to the parent.

title: Unique identifier used to retrieve child profile
description: The Authentication Service shares a unique child identifier or login credential in the read request to link and retrieve the specific child profile from the database.

title: Identifier in query for child login
description: The data flow carries an identifier referencing the child data subject to fetch the profile for authentication.

title: Sensitive child profile data accessed
description: The ChildProfile Database discloses highly sensitive personal data of children (minors) for the login process, which requires strict necessity assessment.

title: Child data subject unaware of profile access
description: Children (or guardians) may be unaware that their profile data is being read during login authentication.
uncertainty_note: Flow description provides limited context on awareness mechanisms; this is inferred from child data context.

title: Potential violation of data minimization for child data
description: Reading full child profiles may process more data than strictly necessary for login authentication, conflicting with minimization principles especially for children's data.

title: Email identifier transmitted in login flow
description: The parent login flow sends an email address which serves as a unique identifier for the data subject.

title: Sensitive password data received
description: The authentication service receives a password, which is a highly sensitive data type, as part of the login process.

title: Linking via unique email identifier
description: The email in the login data flow can be used to link the authentication action to the specific parent user.

title: User unawareness when sharing login credentials
description: The parent user sharing email and password may not be fully aware of how this personal data will be processed or stored by the system.

title: Excessive volume of child profile data read
description: The service reads all childprofiles for a parent (find all), processing an excessive amount of personal data beyond what may be functionally needed for a specific operation.

title: Processing of identified child profile data
description: The flow involves reading childprofiles by id or for parent, which includes identified or identifiable personal data of children.

title: Sensitive child data stored and disclosed on read
description: The ChildProfile Database stores and provides highly sensitive personal data about children upon read requests.

title: Linking child profiles to parent via unique identifier
description: Reading childprofiles for parent using id links the data to specific parents and children through unique identifiers.

title: Processing of identified child subprofile data
description: The Children Subprofile Service receives and processes identified personal data (name, age, idImage) to create a child subprofile.

title: Sensitive data type collection for child subprofile
description: idImage represents a highly sensitive data type (identity document image) that may exceed strict functional necessity for subprofile creation.
uncertainty_note: Exact sensitivity depends on what idImage precisely contains, but ID imagery is typically sensitive.

title: Unawareness when sharing child personal data
description: The parent user sharing child data (name, age, idImage) may lack full awareness of processing implications, storage, or downstream uses for the child's subprofile.

title: Potential data minimization violation for child data
description: Collecting idImage along with name and age for a child subprofile may process more personal data than strictly necessary, especially given children's data protections.
uncertainty_note: Depends on exact system requirements for subprofile creation.

title: Storing identified child profile data
description: The ChildProfile Database receives and stores identified personal data including name, age, idImage path for children.

title: Sensitive child data types stored
description: Storing child profiles with name, age, image path and approved videos involves highly sensitive personal data of minors.

title: Potential data minimization violation for child profiles
description: Writing full child profiles (including image paths) to the database may process more data than strictly necessary without clear justification in flow.
uncertainty_note: Flow description does not specify necessity or minimization controls.

title: Propagation of child profile data
description: The Children Subprofile Service propagates personal child data to the database which may expose it beyond immediate need.

title: Sensitive personal image data stored in file upload
description: The destination DataStore receives and stores idImage file uploads (children subprofile images) to backend/uploads/images. Images of children constitute highly sensitive personal data that may not be strictly necessary or should be minimized.

title: Processing and sharing of identified image data
description: The Children Subprofile Service (source) shares idImage file uploads, which likely contain or are linked to identified personal data of children.

title: Linking via image identifier in transit
description: The data flow carries idImage which serves as a unique identifier allowing linking of the image data to specific child subprofiles.

title: Sensitive personal data in video upload
description: Video file contains visual personal data (e.g. faces, scenes) that may be highly sensitive depending on context, disclosed upon upload to the service.

title: Revealing attributes in uploaded content
description: Title, description and video content include attributes that can reveal identity of the parent user or others depicted.

title: Metadata evidence of upload action
description: Flow metadata or video metadata creates attributable evidence of the upload action that cannot be repudiated.

title: Unawareness of video processing
description: Data subject (parent) may remain unaware of how the uploaded video, title and description will be stored, analyzed or further disclosed by the Video Service.

title: Linking via uploader identifier in metadata
description: The data flow carries uploader information as part of video metadata, which serves as a unique identifier allowing linking of this video data to the specific user across records or sessions.

title: Identified information in video metadata
description: Video metadata written includes uploader details, which constitutes identified information being processed and stored via this flow.

title: Metadata enables attribution and non-repudiation
description: Storing uploader metadata in the database creates attributable evidence of the upload action, preventing the user from denying involvement with that video.

title: Stored video file as attributable evidence
description: Writing the video file to persistent storage creates a data record that can be attributed to a data subject, preventing denial of involvement or claims about the content.
assumptions: Video file originates from or depicts a data subject
uncertainty_note: Flow description does not explicitly confirm personal data or user association in the video file

title: Indefinite retention of video files
description: Video files are written to storage without any indicated retention limit, leading to personal data being kept longer than functionally necessary.
uncertainty_note: No retention policy mentioned in flow description

title: Lack of erasure control for stored videos
description: Data subjects may lack ability to request removal of their video files from the storage after upload.
assumptions: Videos are personal data of data subjects
uncertainty_note: Flow provides no information on data subject rights implementation

title: Storage limitation principle violation risk
description: Persistent storage of video uploads risks violating storage limitation if no deletion policy is enforced.
assumptions: Video files qualify as personal data
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual implementation details not provided in flow

title: Request includes identified user data for my-videos
description: The Video Service sends read requests to the Video Database that include user identifiers (e.g., for 'my-videos' queries) to fetch personal video lists, processing identified data.

title: Query flow carries unique user identifier
description: The data flow for reading videos (including my-videos and by id) transmits unique references like user IDs or video IDs that can identify the data subject.

title: Database access propagates personal video data
description: The Video Database makes personal videos accessible to the Video Service beyond strict functional needs for list/search operations.

title: Users unaware of video data reads
description: Data subjects may be unaware that their video lists and searches are being read/processed from the database by the service.

title: Processing of identified user data via findById
description: The User Management Service (P2) requests and processes identified data when performing read/update operations on user profiles or roles using findById and findByIdAndUpdate, directly handling unique user identifiers and associated personal profile information.

title: Linking via unique identifier in database query flow
description: The data flow DF16 transmits unique identifiers (user IDs) as part of findById/findByIdAndUpdate operations between the service and database, enabling direct linking of queries and updates to specific individuals.

title: Storage of identified user profile data
description: The User Database (DS1) receives and stores identified personal data including user profiles and roles as a result of the read/update operations over this flow.

title: Processing of identified data for user management
description: The User Management Service processes identified data (e.g., user identifiers) to update roles or delete specific users.

title: Linking via unique identifiers in admin actions
description: The data flow links admin actions to specific users through unique user identifiers for role updates or deletions.

title: Attributable admin actions on user data
description: Admin's update or delete actions create attributable evidence that can prevent denial of performing these operations on user accounts.

title: Unawareness of affected data subjects
description: Users subject to role changes or deletion may remain unaware of the processing of their personal data by the admin action.

title: Prolonged retention of auth data in local storage
description: Auth token and user object stored in browser local storage may persist longer than needed for authentication functionality, violating storage limitation.

title: User unaware of browser storage of personal data
description: Authentication service returns user object and token for local storage without mechanisms to inform data subject about persistent client-side storage of their data.

title: Increased accessibility via local storage
description: Flowing the auth token and user object to local storage makes the personal data broadly accessible to client-side code and potentially other parties with browser access.
